title: Mechanical Thrombectomy With Dual Stents vs. Single Stent in Acute Ischemic Stroke (TWIN2WIN-2)
official: Randomized Clinical Trial to Compare the Efficacy of Mechanical Thrombectomy Using a Dual-Stent Retriever Versus the Conventional Single-Stent Technique as a First-Line Treatment in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
summary:
The TWIN2WIN-2 study is a randomized clinical trial that aims to compare two techniques used in mechanical thrombectomy, a treatment performed on patients with acute ischemic stroke (a type of stroke caused by a blockage in a brain artery).

Specifically, the study compares the use of a single stent retriever (a small metal mesh used to remove the clot from the blocked blood vessel) with the use of two stent retrievers simultaneously, both as a first-line treatment.

The primary objective is to determine whether the use of a dual-stent retriever improves patients' clinical recovery 90 days after the stroke, as assessed using a scale called the Modified Rankin Scale (mRS), which measures the degree of disability or dependence in daily activities.

In addition, the safety of the procedure will be evaluated by monitoring for complications such as cerebral hemorrhages, as well as its efficacy in terms of successfully reopening the artery on the first attempt.

Between 5 and 10 stroke centers will participate, and the study is expected to include 402 adult patients. Each participant will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. Follow-up will include assessments at 24 hours, at hospital discharge, and at 90 days.

The study is designed to improve care for stroke patients and help determine which technique yields the best results from the very start of treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria: Age ≥ 18 years

Informed consent from the patient or a representative

Disabling focal neurological deficit consistent with acute cerebral ischemia

Baseline NIHSS ≥ 6

Pre-stroke mRS of 0 or 2

Treatable within 24 hours of symptom onset

Treatment with IV t-PA if indicated

TICI 0-1 occlusion in the terminal ACI, distal M1, or basilar artery, confirmed by angiography

NRI trained in DS-EVT

\-

Exclusion Criteria:

* mRS \> 2 prior to stroke

Use of another thrombectomy device

Bilateral or multiple strokes

Hemorrhagic diathesis, INR \> 3.0, platelets \< 50,000

Severe or terminal illness (\<6 months to live)

Intracranial tumors, cerebral vasculitis, active infection

Cocaine use, pregnancy, breastfeeding

Participation in another interfering study

ASPECTS \<6 or \<5 on MRI

Imaging evidence of hemorrhage, occlusive dissection, or mass with midline shift

Underlying intracranial atherosclerosis, multiple affected territories

Suspected septic embolism, endocarditis

Difficulty with 90-day follow-up
